78.question_text: Consider the statements: (1) If p > 2 is prime, it can be written as 4n + 1 or 4n + 3 for a suitable natural number n. (2) If p > 2 is prime, (p − 1)(p + 1) is always divisible by 4. Which statement is true?
solution_steps: The value 3 cannot be written as 4n + 1 or 4n + 3 for any natural number n, so statement 1 is false.
For p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, and so on, (p − 1)(p + 1) is divisible by 4, so statement 2 is true.
Hence, statement 1 is false and statement 2 is true.

344.question_text: Let N = 1! + 2! + 3! + … + 99! + 100!. Find the last two digits of N.
solution_steps: The terms 10! + 11! + … + 100! have 10! as a factor and therefore end in 00.
So the last two digits of N are the last two digits of 1! + 2! + … + 9!.
1! + 2! + … + 9! ends in 13. Therefore, the last two digits of N are 13.

353.question_text: If [x] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to x, find [1/4] + [1/4 + 1/50] + [1/4 + 2/50] + … + [1/4 + 49/50].
solution_steps: The first 38 terms, from [1/4] through [1/4 + 37/50], have values between 0 and 1 and therefore contribute 0 each.
The remaining 12 terms, from [1/4 + 38/50] through [1/4 + 49/50], have values between 1 and 2 and therefore contribute 1 each.
Hence, the expression equals 0 × 38 + 1 × 12 = 12.
